description:
FILED s473w (Opus, 2026-09-09) from the #1502 CPAN-board census probes.

SILENT WRONG.  A `/g` match whose TARGET is an element of `@_` matches, but
records NO `pos` â neither inside the sub nor on the caller's variable the
element aliases.  Every other spelling of the same match records it.

REPRODUCER (probed vs perl 5.40.3; PCL is the second column):

    sub m_G_gc  { my $r = ($_[0] =~ /\Gabc/gc) ? 1 : 0;
                  return "$r/" . (defined pos($_[0]) ? pos($_[0]) : 'undef') }
    sub m_gc    { ... /abc/gc ... }
    sub m_g     { ... /abc/g  ... }
    sub m_lex   { my $x = $_[0]; ... /\Gabc/gc on $x ... }

    my $a = "abcdef"; print m_G_gc($a), " outer=", pos($a) // 'undef';

                 perl          PCL
      G_gc       1/3 outer=3   1/undef outer=undef
      gc         1/3 outer=3   1/undef outer=undef
      g          1/3 outer=3   1/undef outer=undef
      plain      1/undef       1/undef              <- agrees (no /g, no pos)
      lex        1/3           1/3                  <- agrees (lexical copy)

So the match SUCCEEDS (the boolean is right) and only the pos side-effect is
lost, which is the worst shape: a scanning loop
`while ($_[0] =~ /\G.../gc) { ... }` never advances and either spins or
silently reads the same token forever.

The `\$_[0]` spelling WORKS (`sub f { my $r = \$_[0]; $$r =~ /\Gabc/gc;
pos($$r) }` gives 3 inside and 3 outside, identical to perl) â which is why
Text::Balanced, whose extract_* family opens with `my $textref = \$_[0]`, is
NOT an instance of this bug (that family is #1568).

WHERE TO LOOK: the pos state is attached to the BOX, and an `@_` element is
reached through `(p-aref @_ N)`.  Compare with the lexical path, which is the
one that works.  A raw (unboxed) element cannot carry pos at all, so the fix
is probably the s455 element model's promote-at-alias-event rule: a `/g` match
target is an alias event.

NOT MEASURED: how many board or sweep rows sit behind it.  The census found it
by probing the Text-Balanced cluster and it is filed on its own merits.
subject: SILENT WRONG: a /g match on an @_ ELEMENT (`$_[0] =~ /\Gx/gc`) matches but records NO pos â inside the sub or on the caller variable; the `\$_[0]` and lexical-copy spellings both work
